title: Height-Balanced Dispatch and Stack Invariants in a C-Based Stack-Based Bytecode Virtual Machine
topic: Build Your Own Stack-Based Bytecode Virtual Machine in C
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a compact, formally analyzable stack-based bytecode virtual machine (VM) implemented in C. The VM employs a height-balanced binary search tree to index opcode handlers, guaranteeing $O(\log M)$ dispatch time for $M$ distinct opcodes, while stack operations remain $O(1)$. We prove that the stack depth never exceeds the allocated capacity and that the tree height satisfies the classic red-black bound. Static abstract syntax tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 186 source lines and a single function block, with an auxiliary memory footprint of $O(N)$. The design is fully reproducible; source code is available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261119_170533_build_your_own_stack-based_byt}.
